meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'handsome guy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is super, just such a handsome man!
He did a great job, a real handsome guy!

examples.text: Новый официант считает себя главным красавчиком ресторана.
examples.trans: The new waiter considers himself the main handsome guy of the restaurant.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rabbit' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Gratin, please. And rabbit for me.

meanings.note: Locative в лесу after в/на. Common masculine noun meaning 'forest, woods' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давайте поедем в лес на шашлыки!
examples.trans: Let's drive out to the forest for shashlik!

examples.text: Давайте поедем в лес на шашлыки! Даню вон с собой возьмём.
examples.trans: Let's drive out to the forest for shashlik! We will take Danya here along with us.

examples.text: Смотри, дядя Даня, видишь, побелел! Испугался он зимнего леса.
examples.trans: Look, Uncle Danya has gone pale, see! He is afraid of the winter forest.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, little').
Common masculine noun meaning 'bears' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: In the woods among the bears.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть медведь.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always bears.

meanings.note: praise, said to a man, woman or child
Old-fashioned. Common masculine noun meaning 'well done; good person' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I see, I see, you're a hero. Well done.

meanings.note: the person who likes is in the dative: мне нравится = I like it

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to organize'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Understood, chef, we will organize everything.
I will quickly organize everything right now.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: кого-то за что-то = someone for something

examples.text: Но я просто не знаю, как вас поблагодарить.
examples.trans: But I just don't know how to thank you.
She thanked him for his help.
I would like to thank the chef personally.

meanings.note: Поздравляю! = congratulations!. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to congratulate', paired with 'поздравить'.
On foot. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.
